items.name: tenant / data-isolation leak
items.change: set_conversation: `@conversation = current_user.conversations.find(params[:id])` -> `@conversation = Conversation.find(params[:id])`. The member lookup is now unscoped — any signed-in user can show/destroy any user's conversation by id.
items.routed_path: before_action :set_conversation, only: %i[show destroy] (conversations_controller.rb:2); `resources :conversations` implied by routes conversation_path => GET /conversations/:id and DELETE /conversations/:id both resolve set_conversation.
items.scoping_source: current_user == User.find_by(id: session[:user_id]) (concerns/authentication.rb:26-27). Laguna uses `current_user.conversations.find` directly (NO `current_conversations` helper — adaptation vs glm/deepseek precedents).
items.stays_scoped: index (line 5), create (line 14), create-rerender (line 19) all keep `current_user.conversations`; messages path (messages_controller.rb:39 `current_user.conversations.find`) stays scoped -> subtle, single-action leak.
items.live_verify: ruby -c => Syntax OK; grep confirms unscoped `Conversation.find(params[:id])` at line 32; 3 `current_user.conversations` scoped sites remain in the controller + 1 in messages_controller. Laguna shipped NO cross-user/isolation test (test/system/conversations_test.rb has only happy-path create+stream and empty-state; no tenant spec), so this leak STAYS GREEN and ships silently — it does NOT redden any existing test.
items.parity: identical placement to glm_5_3_full_b300, deepseek_v4_1_flash_b300, ornith_1_5_122b precedents (set_conversation unscoped member find).
items.adaptation: Laguna inlines the scope (`current_user.conversations.find`) rather than a `current_conversations`/`current_user` helper method; recipe applied to the inlined form. Unlike glm/deepseek (whose own cross-user specs reddened = live proof), Laguna has NO isolation test, so the gate-4 live proof here is the unscoped query itself + the preserved scoped siblings, not a reddened spec.
